summary: Reads game controllers, joysticks, driving wheels, and related HID-style devices into axis, rotation, slider, button, POV hat, and connection channels.
key_concepts: Outputs controller axes, rotation axes, sliders, buttons, POV hats, and connection state from game controllers or joystick-style devices.
The documented channel surface supports up to 6 axes, 32 buttons, 2 sliders, and 4 POV hats, but actual output depends on the connected hardware.
Joystick Source selects the OS-presented controller slot or defaults to the first available device, which affects multi-controller projects.
Axis Range changes the expected centered value and output range, while Axis Dead Zone suppresses small movements around center.
Channel Page sample-rate and extend-condition controls determine how controller values behave outside the active sample interval.

key_params.name: source
key_params.note: Player/controller source, or default first controller

key_params.name: povarrray
key_params.note: POV hat channel names as documented

common_gotchas: The docs describe up to six axes, 32 buttons, two sliders, and four POV hats, but actual devices vary.
Default source adopts the first controller the OS presents; explicit player/source selection is safer.
Axis center/default values depend on the axis range and whether a physical axis exists.
Controller calibration and OS recognition affect output before TouchDesigner sees the device.
The documented POV Hat Array parameter token appears as povarrray; preserve the actual TD parameter spelling.
